rationale: Same package name, nsURI, and nsPrefix; classifier contents were substantially refactored.
The former abstract root became concrete and absorbed representation formerly supplied by subclasses.
Numeral's required integer value is represented by ArraySize.size after hierarchy flattening.
ConstantValue's property-constant representation is folded into ArraySize.sizeProperty.
Both are required single-valued Integer attributes; the feature was renamed and moved to the flattened ArraySize class.
Both represent a property-based array size, but the feature moved and was renamed, became optional, and its target was generalized from PropertyConstant to ArraySizeProperty.
Same EDataType name, package, and long instance class.
New abstract classifier used to generalize property-backed array-size values.
Same classifier identity, but the Left version newly inherits from ArraySizeProperty.
Same EClass name, owner, flags, supertypes, and declared features.
The former ArraySize subtype for references to Property has no compatible Left counterpart; ArraySize.sizeProperty targets ArraySizeProperty, which Property does not inherit.
The required Property reference was removed with PropertyReference; no Left reference has the resolved target Property.
Same abstract domain class, but its contained array representation changed from one ArraySpecification to multiple ArrayDimension objects.
Both are containment references describing array shape; the name and target changed and multiplicity changed from default 0..1 to 0..*.
The aggregate specification was replaced by a per-dimension object, shifting repetition to ArrayableElement.arrayDimension.
Both are containment references to ArraySize, but the declaration moved to the per-dimension class and multiplicity changed from 0..* to default 0..1.
The required integer dimension count was removed; Left instead represents dimensions through the multiplicity of ArrayableElement.arrayDimension.
